title: MIsCORE-RIUD: Paper VIII Horizon Formation, Relaxation, and the GR-Side Mechanism From Residual Internal Time to a Replicated Pre-AhC Source Landmark, Dynamical-Horizon Balance, and a Frozen Forward Detector Test
content: MIsCORE-RIUD is a residual-first observational program that treats structured post-model data as an unresolved data layer rather than assigning it to noise or new physics before its organization is tested. Earlier papers established recurrent merger-local population morphology, H1/L1 local common support, connected multiscale paths, intrinsic registration of heterogeneous events onto a common internal progression coordinate, a recurrent state system, a structural GAP, and a frozen transition-rate law. The coordinate is not a cosmetic normalization: equal nominal event time does not guarantee the same internal dynamical stage across heterogeneous mergers. Paper VIII asks what physical evolution underlies that organized population progression and whether it survives from residuals to unsubtracted detector strain and then to source-native general relativity. The RAW bridge was obtained only after a stronger route failed. A blind event-specific RAW/source landmark search did not yield stable population-wide independent landmark recovery, and that negative result is retained. Conditioning only on the already-frozen GAP, a 95-event complete-join RAW audit identifies a multiplicity-corrected L1 20-100 Hz envelope log-jump transition: GAP-minus-PRE median -0.0312953 with studentized Z = 7.2154 and max-T p = 0.0050, and GAP-minus-POST median +0.0244377 with max-T p = 0.0098. The relation extends across a +/-20 ms neighborhood, whereas event-coordinate shuffle does not support unique eventwise GAP binding (best max-T p = 0.8824). The supported RAW statement is therefore a common merger-neighborhood transition, not a point singularity. Source-native numerical relativity provides a second representation change. In an exploratory ten-simulation SXS cohort, the frozen detector-like center-versus-flanks law localizes on the pre-common-horizon side, near AhC-25M. The candidate location was frozen and then reproduced without retuning in five additional SXS simulations: H1-like, L1-like, and joint responses are positive in 5/5. Across the combined SXS15 cohort, a fixed -35,-30,-25,-20,-15M stencil shows coherent acceleration of h22 amplitude growth, h22 frequency growth, binary separation decrease, and infall in 15/15 sources. At the fixed -25M location, the joint detector-like response is associated with h22 amplitude across SXS15 (Spearman rho = 0.7179, permutation p = 0.00347; 12-test Bonferroni bound approximately 0.0417). The supported source interpretation is a reproducible pre-AhC plunge/infall landmark, not equality between GAP and a horizon field. The residual coordinate is projected onto the source-time axis by a frozen two-anchor affine map, MT -> 0M and GAP -> -25M. Independently, 2,976 frozen R40 rows across 96 events yield a common-axis state/rate trajectory and an exact serialized decomposition of the transition hazard. The main state-reorganization transitions occur earlier than GAP, whereas GAP and MT lie predominantly inside the G state while eta, lambda, and p decline through the later high-G interval. The exact producer decomposition reconstructs ETA to machine precision, supporting the interpretation of the frozen generator as an internal-time rate law without requiring pointwise SXS state identity. The GR-side mechanism is tested separately in a controlled Einstein Toolkit binary-black-hole calculation. The producer-native vacuum Ashtekar-Krishnan balance recovers 98.6656% of the observed areal-radius growth over the canonical 0.25-0.50M interval, with 72.4946% from shear and 26.1709% from the 2-zeta term. A fresh local-phase extension maintains percent-level closure through 2M (1-2M trapezoid 99.917%; 0-2M trapezoid 99.151%). A separate same-run Psi4 calculation provides outgoing source-waveform output. A final forward bridge tests whether the source-side construction can survive projection back toward detector space. A B06 190M numerical-relativity branch supports source-to-detector forward generation and R30/R40 extraction robustness, but exact observed-GW150914 identity is not available and a strict full historical replay is not executable under the surviving input-domain contract. A posterior-conditioned GW150914 analogue was therefore frozen independently of observed RAW. Forensic reconstruction then showed that an initial separate-detector comparison used a different operator than the historical R0 quantity and could not be interpreted as an R0 failure. Under the recovered R0 H1/L1 joint operator, a new same-operator forward test gives synthetic R30/R40 landmark positions of 20, 18, and 8 ms at widths 5, 10, and 20 ms, compared with observed positions 4, 14, and 7 ms, corresponding to absolute offsets 16, 4, and 1 ms. Historical R0 parity remains not identifiable because the original HDF5 universe is incomplete; the new result is therefore classified as partial forward positional support, not exact microscopic closure. Taken together, Paper VIII is not merely a GR appendix to RIUD. It unifies the population phenomenon, its residual-space internal-time dynamics, a distinct RAW frequency-activation and spectral-redistribution relation, a replicated pre-AhC source progression, post-AhC dynamical-horizon balance, outgoing radiation, and a limited same-operator forward detector return. These quantities are not algebraically identical. The central result is that representation-specific laws and observables can remain organized by one higher-order merger progression once heterogeneous events are compared through the frozen common coordinate and landmarks.
